title: Norwegian Lamb Couscous Pilaf
description: A pungent and tender Norwegian dish featuring lamb, couscous, and a blend of spices, perfect for a special occasion. This recipe is gluten-free friendly and showcases the unique flavors of Norway.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 300 degrees Fahrenheit.
In a large bowl, toss the lamb pieces with salt, pepper, and thyme until they are evenly coated.
Heat the olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat and sear the lamb until browned on all sides.
Add the chopped onion to the pot and cook until it is translucent and starting to caramelize.
Add the garlic to the pot and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly to prevent burning.
Add the chicken broth to the pot and bring to a boil, then cover the pot and transfer it to the preheated oven.
Bake the lamb mixture for 2 1/2 hours, or until the lamb is tender and falls apart easily.
About 30 minutes before the lamb is done, prepare the couscous according to the package instructions.
Fluff the cooked couscous with a fork and stir in any remaining liquid from the lamb mixture.
Serve the lamb over the couscous, garnished with fresh herbs if desired.
Ensure poultry is cooked to an internal temperature of 74°C / 165°F (juices run clear, no pink remaining) before serving.
